caption_used: Comparison of per-output and per-layer perplexity at different sparsity rates using a logarithmic scale. Both pruning configurations maintain comparable perplexity below 10^1 for sparsity rates up to 50%, after which values begin to diverge. At 60% sparsity, the Per-Output configuration reaches approximately 15 while Per-Layer remains near 10^1. The most pronounced separation occurs at 70%, where Per-Output perplexity climbs to roughly 50 while Per-Layer reaches approximately 25. At 80% sparsity, both configurations approach 10^3, with Per-Output exhibiting marginally higher perplexity than Per-Layer at this extreme.

raw_responses.Bulgarian: DESCRIPTION: The figure is a grouped bar chart comparing two pruning configurations — “Per-Output” (blue bars) and “Per-Layer” (orange bars) — in terms of perplexity across eight discrete sparsity rates: 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80%, listed along the horizontal axis labeled “Sparsity Rate.” The vertical axis, labeled “Perplexity,” is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 to 10^3, with major gridlines at 10^0, 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. For each sparsity rate, two adjacent bars represent the respective perplexity values of the two configurations. At sparsity rates from 10% to 50%, both configurations exhibit perplexity values below 10^1, with the bars visually similar in height. At 60% sparsity, the Per-Output bar rises to approximately 15, while the Per-Layer bar remains close to 10^1. At 70%, the Per-Output bar reaches approximately 50, and the Per-Layer bar reaches approximately 25. At 80% sparsity, both bars approach 10^3, with the Per-Output bar slightly taller than the Per-Layer bar. The legend in the upper left corner identifies the blue and orange bars as “Per-Output” and “Per-Layer,” respectively. No additional annotations, error bars, or visual emphasis (such as shading or outlines) are applied to any bars.
raw_responses.Chinese:
This bar chart visually compares the perplexity performance of two pruning strategies—“Per-Output” and “Per-Layer”—across eight discrete sparsity rates ranging from 10% to 80%, with the vertical axis representing perplexity on a logarithmic scale from 10^0 to 10^3. The horizontal axis lists sparsity rates in 10% increments, ordered left to right from lowest to highest. Each sparsity rate is represented by a pair of adjacent vertical bars: blue for “Per-Output” and orange for “Per-Layer,” as indicated by the legend in the upper left. At 10% sparsity, both bars are near 10^0 (approximately 5–6). As sparsity increases to 50%, both configurations remain below 10^1, with values hovering around 7–9. At 60% sparsity, the “Per-Output” bar rises to approximately 15 while “Per-Layer” remains near 10. At 70%, “Per-Output” reaches roughly 50 and “Per-Layer” approximately 25. At 80% sparsity, both bars approach 10^3, with “Per-Output” slightly taller than “Per-Layer,” indicating marginally higher perplexity. The bars are grouped by sparsity rate, with no stacking, and are uniformly spaced. No bars are visually emphasized with shading, outlines, or annotations beyond the standard color coding and axis labels.

raw_responses.English:
This bar chart illustrates a comparison of perplexity values for two pruning configurations—Per-Output and Per-Layer—across increasing sparsity rates from 10% to 80%, with the y-axis representing perplexity on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 to 10^3 and the x-axis displaying sparsity rate categories in 10% increments. The chart features grouped vertical bars for each sparsity rate, with blue bars denoting Per-Output and orange bars denoting Per-Layer, as indicated by the legend in the upper left. At sparsity rates of 10% through 50%, both configurations exhibit perplexity values near or below 10^1, with bars of nearly equal height. At 60% sparsity, the Per-Output bar rises to approximately 15 while the Per-Layer bar remains close to 10^1. At 70%, the Per-Output bar reaches roughly 50 and the Per-Layer bar approximately 25, showing a clear divergence. At 80% sparsity, both bars approach 10^3, with the Per-Output bar slightly taller than the Per-Layer bar. The bars are arranged in ascending order of sparsity rate along the x-axis, and no additional visual emphasis such as shading or annotations is applied beyond the color-coded grouping and logarithmic axis scaling.

raw_responses.German: DESCRIPTION: Das Balkendiagramm vergleicht die Perplexität von zwei Pruning-Strategien — „Per-Output“ und „Per-Layer“ — bei unterschiedlichen Sparsitätsraten, wobei die Perplexität auf einer logarithmischen Skala dargestellt wird. Die horizontale Achse zeigt die Sparsitätsrate in Prozent, aufgeteilt in acht Kategorien von 10 % bis 80 % in 10 %-Schritten, und ist kategorisch angeordnet. Die vertikale Achse stellt die Perplexität dar, skaliert logarithmisch von 10^0 bis 10^3, mit Tick-Markierungen bei 10^0, 10^1, 10^2 und 10^3. Für jede Sparsitätsrate gibt es zwei nebeneinander angeordnete Balken: ein blauer Balken für „Per-Output“ und ein orangefarbener Balken für „Per-Layer“. Bei Sparsitätsraten von 10 % bis 50 % liegen beide Balken unterhalb von 10^1, wobei die Werte nahe beieinander liegen. Ab 60 % Sparsität steigen die Werte an: bei 60 % beträgt die Perplexität für „Per-Output“ etwa 15 und für „Per-Layer“ etwa 10; bei 70 % steigt „Per-Output“ auf etwa 50 und „Per-Layer“ auf etwa 25; bei 80 % erreichen beide Werte nahezu 10^3, wobei „Per-Output“ leicht höher liegt als „Per-Layer“. Die Balken sind nicht sortiert, sondern nach steigender Sparsitätsrate angeordnet, und es gibt keine visuelle Hervorhebung außer der Farbcodierung gemäß der Legende oben links.
